text:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in GPU OOMs on pool `g4dn-prefill-us-east-1`. 12 OOMs and 7 container restarts in last 4m. Paging on-call @alice. Link: https://alerts.redwood/alert/1726509999 :rotating_light:

alice: saw the page, I'm on it. any quick summary of customer impact?

ben: logs show repeated `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` during prefill stage. stack traces point to kvcache growth + long input sequences (~40k-80k tokens). containers get SIGKILL after kernel OOM, kubelet restarts them. sample log:
```
# /var/log/runtime/pod-xyz.log
2024-07-15T03:01:12Z runtime ERROR: cuda memory alloc failed: out of memory (errno ENOMEM)
2024-07-15T03:01:13Z runtime INFO: container restarted by kubelet (reason: OOMKilled)
```

charu: node `g4dn-23` also flapped once — kubelet restarted and lost pod allocations, causing short capacity dip. kube-events: `NodeNotReady -> NodeReady` within ~90s. not a full node eviction but enough to blow scheduled prefill batches.

frank: initial mitigation idea: 1) temporarily throttle or reject requests with context > 32k tokens at the routing layer, 2) route long-context traffic to a fallback smaller-model variant (quantized) or CPU-fallback, 3) disable large prefill batch merging for the pool to avoid multi-request memory amplification.

alice: agree. can we push a routing rule quickly? Ben/Frank, who's taking push?

ben: I can push a temporary routing override. small JSON rule to set per-request max_context and fallback model (will be live in ~2m after rollout):
```
{
  "match": {"param.context_tokens": ">=32000"},
  "action": {"route_to": "model-small-context-v1", "reject_with": null, "rate_limit": 5}
}
```

ben: applying now -> `POST /routing/overrides` -> 202 Accepted. rolling to edge routers.

dave: support: we're seeing customer reports of truncated replies and some 503s for streaming. high-value customer BoltApps is reporting failed uploads for 2 of 8 requests. taking note for customer comms.

eva: I'll draft a customer-facing note: short outage/partial degradation for very long-context requests. Will ask CS to proactively message BoltApps with mitigation steps and timeline.

charu: infra: also recommend disabling multi-request prefill merging (prefetch coalescing) on the pool to avoid combined KV cache explosion. frank can flip the flag in infra feature flags.

frank: flipping `prefill_coalesce=false` on `g4dn-prefill-us-east-1` now. patch applied to config store.

alice: good. ben, any immediate drop in OOM rate?

ben: OOMs down from 12 -> 3 in last 5m after routing rule + coalesce disable. node flaps stopped. containers still restarting occasionally but less frequent.

charu: watching node metrics: GPU memory pressure fell ~55% on affected pool, reclaim looks healthy.

alice: handing the ongoing watch to night oncall @charu. I'll update the incident timeline and start a brief postmortem draft. Keep this thread for live mitigation notes only.

charu: ACK — I'll keep monitoring for 30m, will escalate if OOMs recur. immediate next steps I own: 1) validate routing rule persists across router restarts, 2) run a targeted smoke test for long-context degrade path, 3) coordinate with infra for a safe kernel/drivers check if flaps reappear.

dave: support will log impacted customers and add BoltApps to high-touch follow-up.

eva: customer note queued, will send once we confirm stable for 10m.

ben: quick note for follow-up: we should add a pre-filter that estimates token footprint before enqueueing prefill and reject early with 413-like error for insanely long sequences (>80k) rather than letting runtime allocate. filing ticket INF-4821.

alice: thanks team. marking this thread as mitigation-in-progress. will close when stable for 30m with no container restarts.

incident-bot: UPDATE: routing override accepted (id r-9f7c). OOM rate decreased. current status: watching.

charu: 1726511400 — 30m watch started. will pulse every 10m here.
